title: gate command's structured details.gate ignores nested ASR sub-result
detail: result.ts's buildGateDetails()/summarize() compute details.gate and gateResults[].status/reasons purely from each JSON entry's top-level VideoGateVerdict status, never reading the nested `asr` object that GateCommand.swift embeds when asrPrompt/expectedScript is passed. Swift's own `failed` flag DOES check asr?.status=="FAIL" and exits non-zero, but a caller branching on details.gate==='PASS' (instead of details.ok/exit code) will see PASS even though the ASR voice-content check failed or (if the Python mlx_whisper bridge crashes and GateCommand.swift's `try?` swallows the error) never ran at all. Always gate on details.ok, and if asrPrompt was requested, verify the returned entries actually contain an `asr` key before trusting a PASS.

title: validateExtraArgs never checks value after `--flag=value` syntax
detail: paths.ts's validateExtraArgs splits `--flag=value` tokens only to get the flag name for the allow-list check, then pushes the WHOLE raw token (value included) into argv with no assertPathAllowed on the value part. Since ltx-video (swift-argument-parser) accepts `--flag=value` for any Option, this is a live escape hatch for path-typed flags (output/input/audio-track/latent/lora/last-frame) to read/write outside repoRoot/outputDir/modelsRoot, defeating the allowed-roots guarantee documented at the top of paths.ts. Fix direction: split on first `=`, run assertPathAllowed on the value half for any path-typed flag, same as the space-separated case.

title: looksPathy heuristic in validateExtraArgs skips bare-word path values
detail: validateExtraArgs's `looksPathy` check (tok.includes('/') || tok==='..' || tok==='.' || (tok.includes('.') && tok.length>4)) is false for bare-word values with no slash and no long-enough extension (e.g. a symlink name). For such tokens on a path-typed flag (--input, --latent, etc.) only rejectFlagLike (leading-dash check) runs — assertPathAllowed is skipped entirely, so a symlink dropped under an allowed root (e.g. outputDir) that points outside all allowed roots passes through unchecked.

title: extraArgs --lora path:strength skips mustExist check that structured loras field enforces
detail: index.ts's structured pathSpecFieldKeys loop strips the `:strength` suffix before assertPathAllowed(..., {mustExist:true}) for the typed `loras` field, but validateExtraArgs (paths.ts) validates the SAME `--lora path:strength` token as one opaque string via assertPathAllowed(tok, roots, {kind:'extraArgs value'}) with no mustExist override — so a bogus/non-existent LoRA path passed through extraArgs is silently accepted where the structured field would reject it. Lower severity than the =-smuggling/bare-word gaps but a real inconsistency between the two enforcement paths for the identical flag.

title: EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW list is never cross-checked against the real CLI by check-flags.ts
detail: scripts/check-flags.ts only diffs commands.ts's typed `fields` against `--help` output; it never inspects index.ts's EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW allow-list. A future Swift flag rename/removal that's only reachable via EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW (not modeled as a typed field), or a stale entry left after deleting a typed field, will not be caught by 'bun scripts/check-flags.ts' (still reports clean) -- it only surfaces later as a runtime Swift ArgumentParser ValidationError. As of this run the list itself is verified clean (asr-prompt/expected-script gate fields are correctly typed fields, not extraArgs entries), but nothing in CI enforces it stays that way.

title: ensureBinary() failures inside runOnce/runLtx bypass the documented details.ok=false contract
detail: runLtx's JSDoc states non-zero ltx-video exit surfaces as details.ok=false (not an exception), implying that's the exhaustive throw/no-throw contract. But `await ensureBinary(onProgress)` in runOnce has no try/catch, so repo-root-not-found, `swift build -c release` failing, or the post-build binary still missing (binary.ts) all throw plain Errors that propagate uncaught out of runLtx. Today's only caller (extensions/pi-ltx.ts) independently wraps the whole runLtx() call in try/catch and converts to {details:{ok:false,error}} -- a mitigation living OUTSIDE index.ts. Any other direct caller of runLtx (unit tests, future CLI commands -- both explicitly named as intended use-cases in the file's own header) gets an unhandled rejection instead of the structured shape. Concretely bites on a fresh checkout where the lazily-compiled Swift binary's first build fails.

title: parseWallSeconds' firstMatch grabs base-gen wall time, silently ignores upscale wall time
detail: native-i2v runs upscale by default (upscale:true), and the Swift binary prints two lines: '✅ wall time: Ns' (base T2I+I2V) and '✅ upscale wall time: Ms' (auto-upscale pass). parseWallSeconds in result.ts uses a firstMatch strategy on substring 'wall time:', which always matches the FIRST (base-gen) line and ignores the second (upscale) line -- so details.wallSeconds under-reports total wall time by the upscale duration with no error or indication a second timing line existed. Any consumer logging/comparing run duration for default native-i2v calls gets a silently wrong number.

title: live-e2e baseline: contract clean, check-flags clean, real ASR gate wiring confirmed working across runs
detail: 2026-07-04 run: contract lane 99 pass/0 fail (5 files, 214 expect(), 434ms); check:flags 12/12 commands fully modeled, no drift. live-e2e: native-i2v ok (800x800, 44.0s wall); gate-asr confirmed --asr-prompt/--expected-script reach the real Swift binary + real mlx_whisper end-to-end (asr key present, status FAIL as expected for a 0.38s smoke clip; transcript='謝謝', detectedLang='en' for a zh prompt -- known short-clip misdetection, not a new bug). 2026-07-05 rerun: contract lane grew to 111 pass/0 fail (5 files, 246 expect(), 488ms); check:flags now 15/15 commands fully modeled, no drift (native-i2v/native-upscale both ✓, matching prior run -- previously-known drift items still not manifesting). live-e2e: native-i2v ok (800x800, 71.7s wall -- slower than the 44.0s prior run, within normal variance for this machine); gate-asr again confirmed real asr key present, status FAIL for the same short-clip reason (contentRatio 0, transcript='謝謝', detectedLang='en'), gate command exited 1 as expected on a genuine FAIL verdict. 2026-07-05 (second rerun, run 2026-07-05T00-59-17): contract lane 115 pass/0 fail (5 files, 252 expect()); check:flags still 15/15, no drift ('✓ No drift.'). live-e2e: native-i2v ok (800x800, 71.2s wall, matches prior run's variance band); gate-asr again confirmed real asr key present, status FAIL for the same short-clip reason (transcript='謝謝', detectedLang='en', contentRatio 0), overall gate exit non-zero as expected (also flagged 'video duration too short'). Use this as the passing baseline for contract+check-flags+live-e2e freshness going forward; test/command counts climb as the package grows so compare shape (all-pass, no-drift) not raw counts.

title: buildGateDetails's doc-promised text-parsing fallback doesn't exist -- silent empty gate result when caller forgets json:true
detail: buildGateDetails's own doc comment in result.ts promises 'Falls back to text parsing if --json wasn't set', but the implementation only does JSON.parse(res.stdout); when that throws (caller didn't pass json:true -- easy to forget since gate's json option defaults to false in commands.ts), entries silently stays [] and details.gate/gateResults end up null/empty even on a genuine gate FAIL, instead of regex-parsing the human-readable '✅/⚠️/❌ STATUS  path' lines the way buildI2VDetails/buildUpscaleDetails do for their own 'gate:' summary line. A caller branching on details.gate (e.g. abort pipeline if FAIL) sees null/gate-inconclusive and silently passes a bad clip through, even though res.exitCode (1) and raw stdout both recorded the failure clearly.

title: native-relay's `variant` field embeds a lora path but is typed string[], bypassing assertPathAllowed
detail: commands.ts's native-relay `variant` field (`--variant name[=lora_path[:strength]]`) is modeled as a plain string[] (no isPath/isPathSpecArray), so validateOptionPaths in index.ts only runs rejectFlagLike (leading-dash check) on it instead of assertPathAllowed on the lora_path portion -- unlike the sibling `loras` field in the same command, which correctly uses isPathSpecArray and gets validated via pathSpecFieldKeys. A value like 'evil=/Users/x/.ssh/id_rsa:1.0' (no leading dash) passes rejectFlagLike untouched and buildArgs emits it straight into ltx-video's argv, letting the Swift binary load an arbitrary out-of-root file as a LoRA checkpoint -- defeats the allowed-roots guarantee every other path-bearing field enforces. Fix direction: parse variant's `name=lora_path[:strength]` shape and route the lora_path portion through the same isPathSpecArray/pathSpecFieldKeys machinery as `loras`.

title: onProgress callbacks are invoked unguarded at multiple call sites across invoke.ts, binary.ts, and index.ts
detail: invokeLtx (invoke.ts) invokes its per-line onProgress callback unguarded inside the child process's stdout/stderr 'data' event handler, outside the surrounding Promise's synchronous call stack -- a throw there is NOT caught by any try/catch and does not reject/resolve invokeLtx's promise, even though invokeLtx's own doc comment promises 'Never rejects -- check exitCode/aborted'. The extension boundary (extensions/pi-ltx.ts) wraps only the `await runLtx(...)` call in try/catch, which does not cover this out-of-band stream callback. Same pattern repeats in binary.ts's buildBinary/buildMetallib, which call onProgress unguarded from spawned processes' stdout/stderr 'data' and 'close' handlers with no try/catch anywhere -- a throwing onProgress during a fresh-checkout auto-build (swift build -c release, minutes-long, many progress lines) causes an uncaught exception from inside the child_process listener rather than rejecting the wrapping `new Promise(...)`, so the promise never settles and the whole agent process can crash instead of runOnce/index.ts's caller getting a rejected promise it already knows how to convert into details.ok=false. index.ts's own runOnce() has a THIRD unguarded call site: `onProgress?.({kind:'progress', text:...})` right before spawning ltx-video (i.e. before invokeLtx is even called), so the same crash risk exists even earlier in the call chain, independent of the invoke.ts/binary.ts sites. Fix direction: wrap every onProgress(...) call site in try/catch (swallow or log-only) in invoke.ts, binary.ts, AND index.ts.

title: buildDetails() switch has no case for native-relay/native-ingredients/native-restyle, falls through to text-only details
detail: result.ts's buildDetails() switch dispatches per-command to a dedicated builder (e.g. buildI2VDetails), but native-relay, native-ingredients, and native-restyle -- all writesOutput:true generation commands with real output paths and wall times, per commands.ts -- are missing from the switch and fall through to buildTextDetails (meant only for read-only text commands like `models`). A successful run of any of these three prints the same 'final: <path>' / '✅ wall time: Ns' formats already parsed for native-i2v/native-t2a, but details.output/extraOutputs/wallSeconds/width/height/gate all stay null. Any caller chaining the produced video/frames/audio into a later step (e.g. gate/upscale) gets nothing instead of the real output path, with no error signal that data was dropped.

title: parseDims() reports pre-override width/height when --last-frame-derives-resolution overrides the requested resolution
detail: result.ts's parseDims() reads dims from the single Swift stdout line '→ native I2V ...: N frames @ fps, WxH, ...', which (per NativeI2VCommand.swift) still interpolates the original --width/--height flags rather than effectiveWidth/effectiveHeight even when lastFrameDerivesResolution:true causes the actual generation resolution to be derived from the last-frame image (e.g. halved base resolution). result.ts has no way to detect the override happened, so details.width/details.height silently report the wrong (requested, not actual) resolution with no error -- a caller trusting these fields for downstream sizing (e.g. matching an upscale target) gets a wrong value.

title: agent-supplied outputDir/modelsRoot tool params become allowed roots themselves, making the allowed-roots guarantee circular
detail: pi-ltx.ts's `outputDir` and `modelsRoot` tool parameters are plain agent-supplied strings that become members of AllowedRoots (paths.ts) with zero validation against a fixed sandbox boundary. Write side: passing outputDir to any writable absolute path outside the repo (e.g. victim's Application Support dir) makes resolveOutputDir/ensureOutputDir accept and mkdirSync it, and assertPathAllowed for the `output` field trivially passes since roots.outputDir IS the attacker-chosen dir -- any generated output (PNG-sequence/WAV/mp4) can overwrite files under that path, fully outside the intended repo/models/output sandbox. Read side: same mechanism via modelsRoot -- setting it to e.g. '/etc' makes assertPathAllowed accept any path under it (loras, lastFrame, audioTrack, inputImage, etc.), so options.loras:['/etc/passwd:1.0'] passes the mustExist check and gets handed to the ltx-video binary as a --lora argument, an arbitrary-file-read primitive whose contents flow into the subprocess and potentially back into stdout/stderr. Fix direction: validate outputDir/modelsRoot themselves against a small set of caller-fixed sandbox roots before admitting them into AllowedRoots, rather than trusting them verbatim.

title: pi-ltx.ts header comment says '12 ltx-video subcommands' but commands.ts models 15
detail: pi-ltx.ts's header comment claims the ltx dispatcher picks a command 'one of 12 ltx-video subcommands', but commands.ts currently models 15 (t2i, native-i2v, native-upscale, native-t2a, native-relay, native-ingredients, native-restyle, segment, i2v, upscale, gate, verify, models, audio-decode, video-decode). The comment is stale from before native-restyle/native-ingredients/native-relay were added and was never bumped -- low-severity but misleads anyone using the header as a quick command-surface count when cross-checking coverage.

title: gate's expectedScript field has no enum constraint; an invalid value silently disables the script-mismatch check instead of erroring
detail: commands.ts types gate's expectedScript as free-form string though only 'traditional'/'simplified' are meaningful. On the Swift side (GateCommand.swift), an unrecognized value becomes `ScriptVariant(rawValue: $0.lowercased())` == nil, which ASRGate.swift then treats as expectedScript:nil -- the whole script-mismatch check is silently SKIPPED rather than erroring. A caller passing a mistyped value (e.g. 'zh-TW' or 'trad' instead of 'traditional') expecting the documented zh-CN-vs-zh-TW guard gets no warning that the flag was invalid, and the exact simplified-when-traditional-expected bug this flag exists to catch slips through undetected.

title: ensureOutputDir()'s mkdirSync in runOnce has no try/catch, surfacing raw fs errors instead of details.ok=false
detail: index.ts's runOnce calls `ensureOutputDir(roots.repoRoot, roots.outputDir)` (paths.ts, which does `mkdirSync(dir, {recursive:true})`) with no surrounding try/catch, unlike ensureBinary's build failure two lines later in the same function which IS caught. If roots.outputDir resolves to a path where a parent segment already exists as a regular file (ENOTDIR), or the output volume is read-only/full (EACCES/ENOSPC), the raw Node fs error propagates uncaught out of runOnce/runLtx, crashing the whole tool call instead of giving the agent the structured details.ok=false result the JSDoc promises for every other kind of run failure. Same family as ltx:ensurebinary-uncaught-throw (uncaught throw inside runOnce bypassing the documented contract) but a distinct locus (mkdirSync vs swift build).
